Repeated facts in a flat file

Unit 2 · Week 1 · Lesson 2 · Suggested 55-minute plan; adjust to local timing.

Prepare: Open the database foundations chapter, equipment-loans-flat.csv, database-foundations-workbook.md and database-foundations-answers.md. Use paper or a school-approved spreadsheet. No SQL installation or student account is needed. Use the fixed reporting date of 8 April 2026. Teacher notes and explained answers are public.

Suggested answers are teacher guidance, not extra assessment tasks. These notes are public.

1. Repeated facts in a flat file

Suggested time: 2 minutes

Instructional strategy: Learning intention

Introduce the equipment desk scenario. Explain how repeated facts can create maintenance problems. Activities are ungraded. Use only the supplied fictional loan records. Suggested timings are flexible. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#database-foundations.

2. Rows and borrowing events

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Individual recall, then partner explanation

No. Each row represents a borrowing event. E02 occurs in L002 and L005, which have distinct LoanIDs and different return statuses. Ask what one row represents before judging repeated identifiers. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#database-foundations.

3. Two loans, one borrower

Suggested time: 6 minutes

Instructional strategy: Worked table and discussion

This extract repeats borrower and item details. In the full CSV, L002 is an active loan due on 8 April and L005 is a returned loan due on 4 April. The rows are legitimate history. Repeated labels create a maintenance risk when the label changes, even though repeated IDs may be necessary. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#database-foundations.

4. An incomplete update

Suggested time: 10 minutes

Instructional strategy: Teacher model with student predictions

Demonstrate on a disposable copy or annotate the two rows on paper. The unchanged BorrowerID identifies the same borrower. Updating only one repeated label leaves an inconsistency. In a suitable relational design, one Borrower record stores the label and loans reference that borrower. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#database-foundations.

5. The final-loan deletion

Suggested time: 10 minutes

Instructional strategy: Paired practice with exchanged roles

Partners inspect the complete CSV. L006 is the only row describing E05 as a Microphone. Removing it loses this register’s only description of that item. Ask students to distinguish losing the loan event from losing an equipment fact. This is a paper simulation, not an instruction to delete the source dataset. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#database-foundations.

6. A separate home for each fact

Suggested time: 12 minutes

Instructional strategy: Independent application

Use workbook questions 5–7. Learners allocate BorrowerID and label to Borrower, EquipmentID and description to Equipment, and LoanID, borrower/item references, DueDate and Returned to Loan. The three sets have 4 borrowers, 5 items and 6 events. This is a responsibility sketch, not a formal ER diagram or the final project schema. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#database-foundations.

7. A repeated identifier

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Choice and explanation

The returned earlier E02 borrowing event disappears. LoanID distinguishes each event. BorrowerID and EquipmentID can legitimately recur in Loan. Separate tables reduce repeated descriptive facts when designed well, but poor links or constraints can still cause errors. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#database-foundations.

8. A change to explain

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Reflection and a fresh example

Flat register: update every occurrence for that borrower consistently. Related design: update the borrower’s one descriptive record and keep the loans referencing its identifier. Ask why changing labels should not erase borrowing history. A CSV may remain adequate for a small temporary list with one editor and manageable checks. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#database-foundations.
